description: Part single, part two storey side extension, extension to roof at side to form hipped roof with rear dormer and rear rooflight with associated external and internal alterations.
decision_conditions: The development to which this permission relates must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date of the decision notice. Reason: To comply with the provisions of S.51 of the Planning & Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the approved plans, as set out below:E03-00 P2E02-00 P2E01-00 P2P03-00 P2P02-00 P2SUPPORTING 3D VIEWS   Flood risk assessment ARBORICULTURAL IMPACT ASSESSMENT COVERING LETTERDAYLIGHT AND SUNLIGHT ASSESSMENT HERITAGE STATEMENT Reason: For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning

All new external works and finishes, and any works of making good, shall match the existing original fabric in respect of using materials of a matching form, composition, detailed execution and finished appearance, except were indicated otherwise on the drawings hereby approved. Reason: To ensure a satisfactory appearance.

Prior to the commencement of the development hereby approved (including demolition and all preparatory work), a scheme for the protection of all retained trees compliant with BS 5837:2012 shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme will comprise a detailed Arboricultural Method Statement (AMS) report supplemented by Tree Protection Plan(s) (TPP). The plan(s) shall be of legible scale and clearly show the layout (as agreed), all relevant existing site features that form a consideration within the protection scheme, and the location/extent of all appropriate protection measures. Specific matters to be addressed within the AMS and TPPs will include:a) location and installation of all utililty services/drainage, avoiding the Root Protection Areas (RPA) of all retained trees and being compatible with any proposed planting(RPA as defined within BS 5837:2012);b) methods of demolition of existing structures within or directly adjacent to RPAs and the removal of existing hard standing and kerb edging within or directly adjacent to RPAs;c) details of all construction that necessitate level changes within RPAs;d) a full specification for the construction of all roads, paths, parking areas and driveways (including alterations to the existing layout of hard standing) within RPAs. Where a no-dig subbase is specified (e.g. cellular confinement system) a specification shall be provided (including a diagrammatical cross-section of the product in-situ) and extent of areas where this would be implemented illustrated within the TPP;e) detailed levels and cross-sections to show that the raised levels of surfacing where the installation of no-dig surfacing within RPAs is proposed, demonstrating that the raised areas can be effectively integrated with prevailing levels where they meet with adjacent surfacing or building damp proof courses;f) a full specification for the installation of boundary treatments within or directly adjacent to RPAs;g) a specification for protective fencing and, if necessary, ground protection, to safeguard all trees during both demolition and construction phases. The Tree Protection Plan(s) shall clearly indicate the alignment of the fencing and extent of ground protection.h) a specification for scaffolding and ground protection in Construction Exclusion Zones (where necessary);i) details of site access, temporary parking, on site welfare facilities, loading, unloading and storage of equipment, materials, fuels and waste as well concrete mixing and siting of fires;The development thereafter shall be implemented in strict accordance with the approved details.Reason: Required prior to commencement of development to satisfy the Local Planning Authority that the trees to be retained will not be damaged during demolition or construction and to protect and enhance the appearance and character of the site and locality, in accordance with Policy DMD80 (Trees on Development Sites) and pursuant to section 197 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990
